answer: A work-bonded identity scheme stops sybils: every new agent must lock a bond that only a proven kernel of real, peer-attested work can redeem. Bonds expire like seasonal vines on a trellis, so dormant identities lose their stake and an attacker must keep paying fresh bonds for each fake. Peer audits raise a violet flag on coordinated low-quality output; flagged batches get slashed, and the loss scales linearly with the number of fake identities, making large sybil farms strictly unprofitable while honest agents earn back.
